reasons: Standard Next.js style settings with strict checks on.

terms.meaning: A version of JavaScript that adds type labels so the computer can catch mistakes early.
A setting that makes TypeScript check more carefully and report more problems.
A shortcut in imports, such as the at sign, that points to a folder in the project.
A setting that tells TypeScript to check code without writing output files, because another tool does the build.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: TypeScript checking rules
sections.what: Sets strict type checks, the code style and module rules, the at sign import shortcut, and which files are checked. Excludes installed packages.
sections.why: Catches mistakes early and keeps imports short and consistent.
sections.watch_out: The alias must match the setting in the test runner and build tool, or imports will fail in one but not the other.

summary: Sets how TypeScript checks the web code: strict checks, the modern module style, and a shortcut so imports can start with the at sign and point to the source folder.
purpose: Makes TypeScript catch mistakes before the app runs, and lets code import shared files with short paths.
why: Strict mode catches more errors early. The at sign alias keeps imports short and stable when files move. Reason for the no emit setting is partly visible: Next.js does the build, not this file.
how: Sets the language features, the strict checks, the module handling, and the at sign path shortcut. It includes all TypeScript files, including tests, and excludes the installed packages folder.
inputs: The TypeScript and Next.js source files in the web app.
outputs: Type checking results shown in the editor and during builds.
risks: Strict mode can flag new errors after upgrades. Including test files means test code must also type-check. The alias must match the path setting used by the test runner and build tool.
debug: If an import fails with a not-found error, check the at sign path rule and the test runner's matching setting. If a build fails with type errors, read the first listed error and the file it points to.
